summary: Carded from a live incident Fabio hit at 16:01Z: connected in download mode (gpu=__cpu__) while a local generation was running, and every model install died. Root cause proven from both sides - the RunPod container log shows hot-store staging a 469MB LoRA then the wrapper Killed with exit 137 OOM on a 3.725 GiB CPU box, and app.log shows the 502, the SSE close with 4 deps outstanding, and remote mode being torn down 2s later by the generation fallback.

note: Claiming js/services/commandExecutor.js, js/services/comfyController.js and routes/downloadManager.js. Fix order follows the causal chain: (1) hot-store must no-op on a __cpu__ Pod - the per-gen call site at commandExecutor:1505 is missing the guard its stage-on-connect twin has at :570, and _remoteVramGb returning null for __cpu__ turns the VRAM size cap OFF on the smallest box; (2) the gen preflight must route local WITHOUT tearing down remote mode when the Pod is noGpu; (3) abandonment must fail the outstanding deps instead of returning silently.

summary: Fabio reported a FOURTH failure from the same incident and named the mechanism himself: 'The UI is showing a mix of being connected to the pod and being local at the same time.' Confirmed by construction - the disconnect edge at shell.js:1554 re-checks INSTALLED state against the local filesystem (MPI-85, correct), but download JOB state is never touched: _depJobs (downloadManager:555) is one unscoped map whose only clear site is cancel-all at :3075, and GET /comfy/downloads/status serves it verbatim. Observed: MiniMax H3 Reference renders '/ INSTALLED' AND an 8% bar at once, and its detail panel shows a frozen '424.7 MB/s - 4.2 / 49.4 GB - ~2 min left' with a live CANCEL. 424.7 MB/s is the Pod's volume rate, not Fabio's connection, so the panel is literally displaying Pod telemetry while the app runs local. Fix 4 lands at the same site as fix 3: failing the outstanding deps on abandonment turns the frozen live readout into a real terminal state.

Fix shipped in 629ab6cb, suite 555/555, mutation-checked - but NOT verified live. Fabio is re-running the exact failing scenario (restart, long generation, connect CPU Pod, retry the same downloads) and the next session reads his result before anything else. Handoff also carries the toast thread he asked to be recorded, including the finding that the Boogu disk-space toast is NOT purely a toast bug: he was installing to the POD, so a remote-intended install was evaluated against LOCAL disk - possibly MPI-539 failure 5 rather than MPI-540 work.
